recipes.name: Brown Rice and Black Bean Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (15 ounce) can green peas, rinsed and drained
1 (14.5 ounce) can Italian-style tomatoes, undrained and chopped
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring the brown rice, water, olive oil, and 1//2 teaspoon salt to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed, 45 to 50 minutes. Scrape into a mixing bowl, fluff with a fork, and refrigerate to room temperature.
Stir the collard greens, black beans, green peas, corn, green chiles, olives, and tomatoes into the cooled rice until evenly mixed. Season to taste with salt and pepper before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Brown Rice and Black Bean Salad
raw_recipe.description: Brown rice, collard greens, and green peas join other vegetables in this colorful salad.

review.reviewBody: I only used the recipe as a guide but it worked really well so I'm giving 5 stars for the great combination and unique salad idea. My version: 2 cups cooked brown rice, 1 bunch collard greens (steamed for 10 minutes and chopped into bite sized pieces), 2 diced tomatoes, 1 and 1/2 cups thawed frozen corn, 2 thinly sliced carrots, 1 cup pinto beans, 4 oz can sliced black olives, 2 finely minced cloves of garlic, 1 diced cucumber, squeeze of lemon, salt & pepper. As you can see mine is just a slight variation of the original because I wanted to use up all the odds and ends I had lurking around the fridge. Thanks for a great recipe idea!

This is a very good base recipe! I've never made a cold rice salad, and it is such a great idea. It just needed some more flavor for our tastes. I used fresh collard greens that I steamed and frozen peas because I don't like canned peas much. I cut this recipe in half, but I still used a full can of tomatoes (Rotel instead of Italian) and used a whole can of jalapeño peppers instead of green chilies. After tasting this, I added 1 t cumin and 2 T lime juice and a good bunch of cilantro. This end result was really good and I'll make it again! Thanks for the great base recipe idea!

Mmmmm good! I microwaved fresh collard greens (5min) and used precooked frozen rice medley to cut down cooking time from 2hrs to 10 min. Added fresh parsley, dried basil, dried oregano, frozen corn, frozen peas, black beans, and garbanzo beans. Only used canned tomatoes. Made a simple red wine vinaigrette and added about half cup to salad. Even my husband loves it! Thanks for great recipe!

Prepared as is, this would have been very bland. Except for frozen peas, I used all fresh veggies, and I added beet greens. I also used quinoa, and roasted fresh green chiles. Since I didn't use "Italian style" tomatoes, I added a sauteed onion and a clove of garlic, along with plenty of fresh oregano. I ended up adding two more cloves of garlic and 1 tsp cumin, and I thought it could have used another onion. The peas seemed out of place, and I don't think the Italian seasonings work with the veggies--this was much better with the cumin added. It did taste better the next day.

An excellent dish that’s healthy and uses brown rice and vegetables. I only had canned black beans, diced tomatoes, corn and peas so added that to the rice per the directions. I added Italian seasoning along with salt and ground pepper and loved it! Will make again for a healthy side dish!

Easy and delicious. Sub'd frozen spinach for collards (it's what I had) and added seasoning (garlic pepper, celery salt...). Next time with olives (didn't have any on hand). Corn on side (one in the house doesn't like corn). Made a lot (there's 4 of us), trying to figure out if I can freeze some.

With a few modifications, this turned out great. I served it as a warm dish. I cooked the rice in a rice cooker and then added the other ingredients to the cooker after the rice was done. I used fresh veggies instead of canned and added cumin and coriander to give it some more flavor.
Added 1/3 cup diced jalapenos. Served w/ grated cheese topping or cottage cheese. Excellent!

This was great! I didn't have canned collard greens, but I had some fresh greens. So I prepared just enough for the salad. I used some left over white corn, used black and green olives, (Didn't have any green chiles). I already had some left over brown rice, used it and mixed everything together and oh my Lord, this was great! I love collard greens and so does my husband! This came out so great....and then it hit me, I forgot to add the left over black beans and the Italian tomatoes! Not to worry, we had some of the salad left over, I'll add these last two ingredients for lunch and really enjoy! Thank you for this recipe! I must make this for company when I host another dinner party! What a wonderful alternative for many items I like! This salad really rocks!!!!

Hi all - this is my recipe, and I've loved reading the comments. I'm thrilled that people are just using this as a springboard to create their own recipe. The point of this is not really to make it exactly as it is written. What's important is the idea that you can take a few base items and add whatever you have on hand. My husband was a Naval Aviator, so I've spent a lot of time traveling, moving, and having unexpected squadron mates show up at my place hungry. Being able to almost instantly create something yummy and filling has always been essential. Over the years living in place like Japan and Italy this recipe has changed according to what I have local - I don't always use canned veggies, but on the fly I can go to the pantry and put this together. It's yummy enough that it's also part of a planned menu rotation and something to keep in the fridge for grain bowls or as a small side. Please keep posting your ideas for others to read! If you're not a rice person just make a bean salad. If you have an instant pot you can cook dried beans quickly without soaking, and those are great as a base. Add fresh veggies. I usually add heat, but I didn't want peppers as part of the base, because some don't like spice - and those that do will find a way to add heat to any dish! Oh, and before someone comments on why I'm rating my own dish as a 5-star I'll tell you. If I were looking for a recipe for ideas I'd give this a 5-star. The intent and (as noted in some of the reviews) adaptability is is great. I'm also counteracting the one person that posted the same 3-star comment twice. I'm fine with whatever rating people give - that's up to them. But, posting multiple mid-star reviews drops the rating incorrectly.
For those needing more spice/flavor I suggest a large fresh, diced jalapeno and 1/2 bunch of cilantro !!
This is pretty decent. It needed a lot of salt to bring out the flavor though. Maybe I'll add some cilantro or cayenne or something next time. It's worth making again though, for sure.
This is pretty decent. It needed a lot of salt to bring out the flavor though. Maybe I'll add some cilantro or cayenne or something next time. It's worth making again though, for sure.
Made as is, it's okay. Made with fresh (or frozen/thawed), it's lovely. Good olives make a difference but you don't need many: just cut em up.
I loved this dish, the hubs, not so much. I would recommend using fresh veggies, sauteed, can veggies can have so much sodium.

Easy to make & not bad...but honestly--didn't thrill me. It was fine, but kind of lame. I added a bit of red pepper flakes & a touch of hot sauce to spice it up, which seemed to help. 

Even though I'd rate it as "fine," most likely won't make this one again.
Substitude aduki beans, fresh cooked collard greens

This recipe is fantastic! Little salt and pepper needed to season. My one change was using frozen peas/corn instead of canned, all else the same and it turned out great. I only made 1/2 the recipe and it still made a large portion.
